item.content:encoded: If you become 554-2, then someone else becomes 554-2, then you'll disappear the next time you're out of line of sight for 5 seconds. You're correct that there's only one instance of -2 at a time, but it's ceasing to be -2 (the last person to view -1) that triggers 554-Boojum. I don't envision it being possible to 'ride it out' by remaining in line of sight until someone else disappears and/or the identity of -1 changes again, if that was what you were wondering - rather, as soon as you're no longer the last person to view -1, you're subject to undergoing 554-Boojum for the rest of your life.

Ooohhhh, that does change the dynamic, doesn't it? much more potential to get out of hand.

…But that mechanism doesn't "click", for me. There is no through-put from instance to instance of -1. Yes, they are both unidentified, but they are not the same corpse. Let's say the current -1 is a child, and the new -1 that replaces it was a professional sumo. Even without IDing either one, they are obviously not the same. So how can a photo that is patently not of the body currently under the whatsit propogate the effect?

I demand fridge-logic! :D

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
-1 always refers to the unidentified body below the machine - you'll note that if you pull it out and identify it another unidentified body forms below the machine (in fact, if 554-Boojum doesn't fire, e.g. because you moved the body first without looking at it, you can get numerous duplicate bodies of the same individual). A photograph of said body that carries the effect doesn't stop being hazardous if the particular instance it represented is replaced, because it's a photo of a then-unidentified instance of 554-1 rather than 'the body of X', and that's what carries the effect.

If an image that did carry the effect was broadcast, as soon as the second person saw it, the first would undergo 554-Boojum, the third person to view it would trigger the event for the second, and so on. The worst-case scenario would be a live broadcast - the broadcast crew would themselves be depopulated, together with anyone from the channel who looked to see what they were doing, with the result that it would continue to be displayed. More people tune in to find out what's happening and are themselves erased. Some people won't disappear right away, as they'll be in line of sight of other people, probably also now instances of -2; but they won't know that's what's keeping them alive, and as soon as they leave the room or go looking for family members who have disappeared they'll be gone too.

item.content:encoded:
-1 becomes inert when removed. Presumably, pictures of them go inert at the same time. If so, when a new victim pops (-2 becomes -1), then all existing danger pictures are rendered safe.

Assuming I haven't completly misunderstood something (never a safe bet), this is a semi-self-containing anomaly. Each information breach would claim, at most, one victim before the effect was again restricted to line of sight. "Nutty" contingency plans and satelite based blindness rays, as awesome as they are, aren't neccesary.

Edit: forgot to mention, I like the containment and I like the item; I just don't like them together. Like chocolate and ham.
